issues.description: push_error is invoked with a string keyword where the framework expects an ErrorFrame.
issues.detail: The author has not stated the precondition of push_error. The PR description claims to 'add error frame for all error types,' yet the call site passes error_msg=... — a string. If push_error's signature requires an ErrorFrame, this is UNREASONED and will fail at runtime on the first error message. Verify the signature before merge.

issues.description: Duplicate literal 'transcriber_error' in the message_type tuple — evidence of unreasoned editing.
issues.detail: 'transcriber_error' appears twice in the elif tuple. The set of error types is a specification artifact; duplication proves it was assembled by copy-paste rather than by enumerating the documented error taxonomy. Harmless to execution, but a tell that the author did not write down and check the precondition.

issues.description: Removing the outer try/except trades one smuggled goto for a silent one.
issues.detail: The old code logged 'WebSocket connection closed' on exception; the new code lets the exception propagate to the websocket_service reconnect loop. Fine — if that loop's invariant is 'exception means reconnect, not crash.' The PR cites the loop but states no invariant proving termination on permanent failure. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: The inner try/except in _receive_messages still swallows all exceptions as 'Error processing message'.
issues.detail: DEFENSIVE-AS-SUBSTITUTE. A bare 'except Exception' wrapping json parsing and dispatch conflates parse errors, dispatch errors, and downstream handler errors into a single log line. The postcondition 'message was processed or a typed error was reported' is not established. Narrow the except, or reason about why every exception class is recoverable here.

issues.description: Error message for non-'error' types falls back to a fabricated string instead of the typed event.
issues.detail: data.get('error', f'Unknown error - {message_type}') assumes the 'error' field exists in every one of the fourteen message types. The ElevenLabs schema almost certainly uses different field names (e.g. 'reason', 'message') per type. The author has not enumerated them. Result: most error frames will read 'Unknown error - rate_limited' even when a payload is present.

issues.description: Changelog file lacks a terminating newline — small, but indicative.
issues.detail: 'No newline at end of file' on a changelog entry is a trivial defect. I note it only because a programmer who does not terminate his text files is a programmer who has not asked 'what is the postcondition of writing this file.' The discipline scales.

review.summary: The patch is a reasonable bug fix smuggled in without a written specification. The infinite-loop diagnosis is plausible but the fix is justified by behavior, not by an invariant — TESTED-NOT-PROVED at best. The expanded error-type list is assembled by copy-paste (duplicate entry, fabricated fallback string, unverified push_error signature) rather than by enumerating the documented error taxonomy and checking each one's payload shape. The intent is correct; the discipline is absent. Acceptable if the P1 items are verified before merge.
